questions.prompt: Which statement best describes self-awareness for a Grade 9 learner?
options: Knowing one's strengths, feelings, values, and areas for growth
Doing only what friends suggest
Avoiding feedback from teachers and parents
Pretending mistakes never happened
questions.correctAnswer: Knowing one's strengths, feelings, values, and areas for growth
questions.explanation: Self-awareness helps a learner understand personal qualities and use feedback to improve.
questions.learningOutcome: Recognize personal strengths, emotions, values, and areas for improvement.

questions.prompt: Which example shows a learner acting according to the value of honesty?
options: Admitting a mistake in group records and correcting it
Copying answers because the work is difficult
Hiding a borrowed item after damaging it
Blaming a classmate for one's own lateness
questions.correctAnswer: Admitting a mistake in group records and correcting it
questions.explanation: Honesty means telling the truth and taking responsibility even when it is uncomfortable.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify how personal values guide responsible choices.

questions.prompt: Why is knowing your learning style useful when preparing for assessment?
options: It helps you choose revision methods that match how you learn best.
It means you no longer need to revise difficult topics.
It proves one method works for every learner.
It allows you to ignore teacher guidance.
questions.correctAnswer: It helps you choose revision methods that match how you learn best.
questions.explanation: A learner who understands personal learning habits can plan revision more effectively.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain how personal learning preferences can improve study habits.

questions.prompt: A learner feels nervous before a public presentation. Which self-awareness action should come first?
options: Name the feeling and identify what is causing it
Leave school without informing anyone
Tell classmates the topic is useless
Refuse to practise because nervousness is permanent
questions.correctAnswer: Name the feeling and identify what is causing it
questions.explanation: Naming a feeling and its cause makes it easier to choose a healthy coping strategy.
questions.learningOutcome: Use self-reflection to recognize emotions and their triggers.

questions.prompt: A teacher says your project is creative but poorly organized. What response best shows a growth mindset?
options: Ask which parts need clearer order and revise the project
Throw away the project and stop trying
Argue that feedback is always unfair
Copy another learner's project exactly
questions.correctAnswer: Ask which parts need clearer order and revise the project
questions.explanation: A growth mindset uses feedback to improve effort, strategy, and results.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply feedback to improve learning and personal development.

questions.prompt: Which action would best help a learner connect talents to future career choices?
options: Compare interests, skills, values, and school subjects before exploring options
Choose a career only because it sounds fashionable online
Ignore weak subjects and avoid asking questions
Let a friend choose the career for them
questions.correctAnswer: Compare interests, skills, values, and school subjects before exploring options
questions.explanation: Career exploration is stronger when a learner connects interests and abilities to real requirements.
questions.learningOutcome: Relate talents, values, and interests to possible career pathways.

questions.prompt: Two learners receive the same low score. One reviews mistakes and seeks help, while the other says they are simply not clever. What is the best analysis?
options: The first learner shows self-efficacy by believing effort and support can improve performance.
The second learner shows better self-awareness because giving up saves time.
Both learners are using the same improvement strategy.
Scores cannot provide useful information for learning.
questions.correctAnswer: The first learner shows self-efficacy by believing effort and support can improve performance.
questions.explanation: Self-efficacy is confidence that one can improve through effort, strategy, and support.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyze how beliefs about ability affect effort and improvement.

questions.prompt: A learner wants to improve leadership but often interrupts others. Which reflection question would be most useful?
options: How does my listening habit affect trust and teamwork?
How can I speak longer so nobody disagrees?
Which classmate should I blame for my behavior?
How can I avoid every group discussion?
questions.correctAnswer: How does my listening habit affect trust and teamwork?
questions.explanation: Good reflection connects personal behavior to its effect on others and points to improvement.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyze personal behavior and its effect on relationships and teamwork.

questions.prompt: Which personal improvement plan best shows self-awareness and realistic action?
options: Identify one weak habit, set a measurable target, ask for feedback, and review progress weekly
Promise to change everything immediately without checking progress
Wait for friends to notice the problem and solve it
Write a long plan but avoid practising the new habit
questions.correctAnswer: Identify one weak habit, set a measurable target, ask for feedback, and review progress weekly
questions.explanation: A useful plan focuses on a clear behavior, measurable action, support, and regular review.
questions.learningOutcome: Create a realistic plan for improving a personal habit or skill.

questions.prompt: A learner is choosing between joining debate club and extra mathematics practice. What should guide the choice most responsibly?
options: Current goals, strengths, time available, and areas that need support
Only what the most popular learners are doing
Avoiding every activity that requires effort
Choosing both without checking the timetable
questions.correctAnswer: Current goals, strengths, time available, and areas that need support
questions.explanation: Responsible choices consider goals, personal needs, and realistic use of time.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply self-knowledge when setting priorities for learning and personal growth.

questions.prompt: What is time management?
options: Planning and using time well to complete important tasks
Waiting until pressure forces you to work
Doing tasks randomly without priorities
Letting other people decide every activity
questions.correctAnswer: Planning and using time well to complete important tasks
questions.explanation: Time management helps a learner organize tasks, avoid waste, and meet responsibilities.
questions.learningOutcome: Define time management and its importance in learning.

questions.prompt: Which item is a SMART goal?
options: I will revise two mathematics topics every evening this week and check ten questions.
I will become perfect in all subjects soon.
I will study whenever I feel like it.
I will improve by hoping for better marks.
questions.correctAnswer: I will revise two mathematics topics every evening this week and check ten questions.
questions.explanation: A SMART goal is specific, measurable, achievable, relevant, and time-bound.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain the features of a clear and measurable goal.

questions.prompt: Why should a learner review a goal before the deadline?
options: To check progress and adjust actions while there is still time
To prove planning is unnecessary
To blame others before results are known
To replace all effort with guessing
questions.correctAnswer: To check progress and adjust actions while there is still time
questions.explanation: Reviewing progress helps a learner correct problems and stay realistic.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain why regular goal review supports achievement.

questions.prompt: A learner has homework, a family duty, and football practice after school. What is the best first step?
options: List tasks, note deadlines, and make a realistic schedule
Do the easiest activity and ignore the rest
Wait until night and rush everything
Skip the family duty without explaining
questions.correctAnswer: List tasks, note deadlines, and make a realistic schedule
questions.explanation: Planning helps balance responsibilities and avoid last-minute pressure.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply planning skills to balance school, home, and personal responsibilities.

questions.prompt: Which strategy best reduces procrastination during revision?
options: Break work into short tasks and start with a timed first step
Wait for perfect motivation before opening a book
Revise only the topics already mastered
Use social media until the deadline is near
questions.correctAnswer: Break work into short tasks and start with a timed first step
questions.explanation: Small timed tasks make starting easier and help build steady progress.
questions.learningOutcome: Use practical strategies to complete tasks on time.

questions.prompt: A learner realizes phone notifications interrupt study every few minutes. What action is most helpful?
options: Keep the phone away or on silent during planned study periods
Answer every message immediately
Study only when the battery is empty
Blame the phone and make no change
questions.correctAnswer: Keep the phone away or on silent during planned study periods
questions.explanation: Managing distractions protects concentration and improves the quality of study time.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply strategies for reducing distractions during learning tasks.

questions.prompt: A group leader notices that one member is doing most of the work while others are idle. What is the best analysis?
options: The group needs clearer roles, fair task sharing, and follow-up.
The active member should do all work because speed matters most.
The quiet members should be ignored until presentation day.
Fairness is not important in group assignments.
questions.correctAnswer: The group needs clearer roles, fair task sharing, and follow-up.
questions.explanation: Self-management in teams includes organizing roles, monitoring progress, and sharing responsibility.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyze how planning and role allocation improve teamwork.

questions.prompt: Which schedule best supports balanced living for a Grade 9 learner?
options: A timetable that includes study, rest, chores, meals, exercise, and sleep
A timetable with study only and no rest
A plan that leaves all work for midnight
A plan based only on entertainment
questions.correctAnswer: A timetable that includes study, rest, chores, meals, exercise, and sleep
questions.explanation: Balanced living protects health while helping a learner meet responsibilities.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyze habits that support a healthy balance between learning and wellbeing.

questions.prompt: Which action plan best prepares a learner for a two-week project deadline?
options: Divide the project into tasks, set dates, gather materials, seek feedback, and revise before submission
Begin the project on the final evening and hope there is enough time
Wait for another group to finish and copy their work
Spend the first week decorating the cover without reading instructions
questions.correctAnswer: Divide the project into tasks, set dates, gather materials, seek feedback, and revise before submission
questions.explanation: A strong action plan breaks work into manageable steps and includes feedback and revision.
questions.learningOutcome: Create an action plan for completing a learning project responsibly.

questions.prompt: Which habit best shows personal responsibility?
options: Completing assigned duties without waiting to be reminded each time
Leaving shared materials for others to clean
Making excuses whenever work is unfinished
Taking credit for work done by classmates
questions.correctAnswer: Completing assigned duties without waiting to be reminded each time
questions.explanation: Personal responsibility means doing what one is expected to do and accepting the results of one's actions.
questions.learningOutcome: Recognize responsible habits in school and home settings.

questions.prompt: What is resilience?
options: The ability to recover and keep trying after difficulty
The habit of avoiding all difficult tasks
The belief that mistakes should be hidden
The refusal to accept help from anyone
questions.correctAnswer: The ability to recover and keep trying after difficulty
questions.explanation: Resilience helps learners face challenges, learn from setbacks, and continue with healthy effort.
questions.learningOutcome: Define resilience and its role in personal growth.

questions.prompt: Why is it important to recognize signs of stress early?
options: Early recognition helps a learner choose support and coping strategies before stress becomes worse.
It makes all school tasks disappear immediately.
It proves the learner is weak.
It removes the need to talk to trusted people.
questions.correctAnswer: Early recognition helps a learner choose support and coping strategies before stress becomes worse.
questions.explanation: Stress signs can guide learners to rest, plan, seek help, or solve the problem safely.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain why early recognition of stress supports wellbeing.

questions.prompt: Which activity is a healthy way to manage anger?
options: Pause, breathe deeply, and discuss the issue respectfully when calm
Insult the person before they speak
Break a shared item to show frustration
Post the conflict online for classmates to judge
questions.correctAnswer: Pause, breathe deeply, and discuss the issue respectfully when calm
questions.explanation: Healthy anger management reduces harm and creates space for respectful problem solving.
questions.learningOutcome: Describe healthy ways of managing strong emotions.

questions.prompt: A learner feels anxious before an exam despite revising. What should they do first?
options: Use calming breathing, review the plan, and arrive prepared
Avoid the exam without informing anyone
Tell others the exam must be cancelled
Stay awake all night without rest
questions.correctAnswer: Use calming breathing, review the plan, and arrive prepared
questions.explanation: Anxiety can be managed through calming techniques, preparation, and realistic thinking.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply coping strategies for anxiety in school situations.

questions.prompt: Your friend has become unusually quiet and has stopped joining group activities. What is the most supportive response?
options: Check on them privately and encourage them to speak to a trusted adult if needed
Mock them until they explain themselves
Share guesses about them in the class group chat
Ignore the change because friends never need support
questions.correctAnswer: Check on them privately and encourage them to speak to a trusted adult if needed
questions.explanation: Supportive friendship includes care, privacy, and guiding someone to trusted help when needed.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply supportive responses when a peer may be struggling emotionally.

questions.prompt: A learner keeps making errors during practice and feels discouraged. Which self-talk statement is healthiest?
options: I can learn from these errors and improve my method.
I am a failure and should stop trying.
The teacher must be against me.
Only perfect learners deserve help.
questions.correctAnswer: I can learn from these errors and improve my method.
questions.explanation: Healthy self-talk encourages effort, learning, and problem solving instead of shame.
questions.learningOutcome: Use positive self-talk to manage discouragement.

questions.prompt: Which situation most clearly requires immediate help from a trusted adult?
options: A learner says they may harm themselves or someone else
A learner dislikes a homework topic
A learner prefers studying alone for one evening
A learner chooses a different library book
questions.correctAnswer: A learner says they may harm themselves or someone else
questions.explanation: Threats of harm are serious safety concerns and should be reported to a trusted adult immediately.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyze situations that require urgent support from trusted adults.

questions.prompt: A classmate laughs loudly during a stressful group task, while another becomes silent. What is the best conclusion?
options: People may show stress differently, so observation and respectful checking are important.
Only silent people experience stress.
Laughter always means a person is careless.
Stress can be measured only by test scores.
questions.correctAnswer: People may show stress differently, so observation and respectful checking are important.
questions.explanation: Stress responses vary, so learners should avoid assumptions and check respectfully.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyze different ways people may express emotions and stress.

questions.prompt: Which peer support plan is safest for a school club?
options: Train members to listen respectfully, protect privacy, and refer serious concerns to a teacher or counsellor
Let learners give medical advice to each other without adults
Ask members to publish emotional problems online
Promise to keep every secret even when someone is unsafe
questions.correctAnswer: Train members to listen respectfully, protect privacy, and refer serious concerns to a teacher or counsellor
questions.explanation: Safe peer support combines empathy with clear referral to qualified adults for serious concerns.
questions.learningOutcome: Create a safe peer support approach for emotional wellbeing.

questions.prompt: Why is enough sleep important for emotional wellbeing?
options: It helps concentration, mood control, and energy for daily tasks.
It makes revision unnecessary.
It prevents every disagreement with friends.
It guarantees a learner will never feel stressed.
questions.correctAnswer: It helps concentration, mood control, and energy for daily tasks.
questions.explanation: Rest supports the brain and body, making it easier to learn and manage emotions.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain the role of rest in emotional and physical wellbeing.

questions.prompt: What is assertiveness?
options: Expressing needs and views respectfully without violating others' rights
Forcing everyone to accept your opinion
Keeping silent even when something is wrong
Using insults to win disagreements
questions.correctAnswer: Expressing needs and views respectfully without violating others' rights
questions.explanation: Assertiveness balances confidence with respect for other people.
questions.learningOutcome: Define assertiveness in respectful communication.

questions.prompt: Which behavior is an example of empathy?
options: Trying to understand how another person feels before responding
Laughing when a classmate is embarrassed
Ignoring a peer who asks for help
Assuming everyone feels exactly like you
questions.correctAnswer: Trying to understand how another person feels before responding
questions.explanation: Empathy means considering another person's feelings and situation.
questions.learningOutcome: Recognize empathy in everyday interactions.

questions.prompt: Why are healthy boundaries important in friendships?
options: They help people respect privacy, safety, time, and personal choices.
They stop friends from ever disagreeing.
They allow one person to control the friendship.
They make communication unnecessary.
questions.correctAnswer: They help people respect privacy, safety, time, and personal choices.
questions.explanation: Boundaries protect dignity and make relationships safer and more respectful.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain why boundaries are needed in healthy relationships.

questions.prompt: Which communication habit best supports teamwork?
options: Listening actively and confirming what others mean before responding
Interrupting whenever you have an idea
Keeping useful information to yourself
Changing the plan secretly without telling the group
questions.correctAnswer: Listening actively and confirming what others mean before responding
questions.explanation: Active listening reduces misunderstanding and helps a team solve problems together.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain communication habits that improve teamwork.

questions.prompt: Why is gossip harmful in a class group?
options: It can damage trust, spread false information, and hurt relationships.
It always solves conflicts quickly.
It proves the speaker is well informed.
It helps absent learners get accurate news.
questions.correctAnswer: It can damage trust, spread false information, and hurt relationships.
questions.explanation: Gossip often spreads unverified claims and can harm dignity and trust.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain how irresponsible communication affects relationships.

questions.prompt: A friend pressures you to exclude a new learner from your group. What is the best response?
options: State that everyone deserves respect and invite the new learner to participate fairly
Follow the pressure to avoid being questioned
Start a rumour about the new learner
Leave the group without explaining the concern
questions.correctAnswer: State that everyone deserves respect and invite the new learner to participate fairly
questions.explanation: Respectful assertiveness helps resist negative peer pressure and supports inclusion.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply assertive communication to resist negative peer influence.

questions.prompt: Two classmates disagree over shared materials during a project. What should they do first?
options: Calmly state the problem and listen to each person's view
Hide the materials until the deadline passes
Ask other learners to choose sides
Stop working and blame the teacher
questions.correctAnswer: Calmly state the problem and listen to each person's view
questions.explanation: Conflict resolution begins by identifying the issue and listening respectfully.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply peaceful steps for resolving disagreements.

questions.prompt: Which response best shows constructive feedback?
options: Your poster is clear, and adding sources would make it stronger.
This is bad, and you should stop presenting.
I liked nothing, but I will not say why.
You are wrong because I prefer my idea.
questions.correctAnswer: Your poster is clear, and adding sources would make it stronger.
questions.explanation: Constructive feedback is specific, respectful, and focused on improvement.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply constructive feedback in peer learning.

questions.prompt: A learner is being mocked repeatedly because of their accent. What should a bystander do?
options: Support the learner, refuse to join the mocking, and report repeated bullying to a trusted adult
Record the mocking and share it for fun
Laugh quietly so the bullies accept them
Tell the learner to ignore it forever
questions.correctAnswer: Support the learner, refuse to join the mocking, and report repeated bullying to a trusted adult
questions.explanation: Bystanders can reduce bullying by supporting the target and involving trusted adults.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply safe bystander actions to prevent bullying.

questions.prompt: A team agrees on roles, but one member keeps missing deadlines without explanation. Which response best protects the relationship and the task?
options: Discuss the issue respectfully, ask what support is needed, and agree on a clear next deadline
Remove the member secretly and insult them in the group chat
Ignore the issue until the presentation fails
Give the member all remaining tasks as punishment
questions.correctAnswer: Discuss the issue respectfully, ask what support is needed, and agree on a clear next deadline
questions.explanation: Responsible teams address problems directly while preserving respect and accountability.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyze respectful ways to address responsibility problems in teams.

questions.prompt: Which statement best compares passive, aggressive, and assertive communication?
options: Assertive communication respects both your rights and others' rights.
Passive communication always solves conflict fastest.
Aggressive communication protects everyone's dignity.
All three communication styles have the same effect.
questions.correctAnswer: Assertive communication respects both your rights and others' rights.
questions.explanation: Assertiveness is clear and respectful, unlike passivity or aggression.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyze the effects of different communication styles.

questions.prompt: A mediator is helping two learners settle a disagreement. Which action should the mediator avoid?
options: Taking sides before listening to both learners
Letting each learner explain without interruption
Helping the learners agree on fair next steps
Keeping the discussion respectful
questions.correctAnswer: Taking sides before listening to both learners
questions.explanation: Mediation requires fairness, listening, and guiding the parties toward a peaceful solution.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyze fair mediation practices for resolving conflict.

questions.prompt: Which class activity best builds inclusion and respect among learners from different backgrounds?
options: A group project where learners share experiences, agree on rules of respect, and solve a common task
A competition where learners mock unfamiliar customs
A seating plan that separates learners by home area
A debate where only one group is allowed to speak
questions.correctAnswer: A group project where learners share experiences, agree on rules of respect, and solve a common task
questions.explanation: Inclusion grows through respectful interaction, equal participation, and shared goals.
questions.learningOutcome: Create inclusive activities that promote respect and cooperation.

questions.prompt: Which plan would best repair trust after a learner spreads false information about a classmate?
options: Admit the harm, apologize privately, correct the false claim, and avoid repeating it
Delete one message and pretend nothing happened
Spread another story to distract the class
Demand forgiveness without changing behavior
questions.correctAnswer: Admit the harm, apologize privately, correct the false claim, and avoid repeating it
questions.explanation: Restoring a relationship requires honesty, repair, and changed behavior.
questions.learningOutcome: Create responsible steps for repairing damaged relationships.

questions.prompt: Why should personal information shared by a friend be kept private unless safety is at risk?
options: Privacy builds trust, but safety concerns should be referred to a trusted adult.
Keeping privacy means never seeking help for any reason.
Friends' information should always be shared for entertainment.
Privacy matters only for adults, not learners.
questions.correctAnswer: Privacy builds trust, but safety concerns should be referred to a trusted adult.
questions.explanation: Respecting privacy protects dignity, while serious safety concerns need adult support.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain how privacy and safety affect trust in relationships.

questions.prompt: What is responsible decision making?
options: Choosing actions after considering facts, values, consequences, and safety
Doing the first thing that feels exciting
Following friends without thinking
Avoiding decisions until others decide for you
questions.correctAnswer: Choosing actions after considering facts, values, consequences, and safety
questions.explanation: Responsible decisions use evidence, values, and likely outcomes before action.
questions.learningOutcome: Define responsible decision making and its key considerations.

questions.prompt: Why should consequences be considered before making a choice?
options: They help predict how the choice may affect self, others, and the future.
They make every choice easy and risk-free.
They matter only after punishment has happened.
They allow a learner to ignore values.
questions.correctAnswer: They help predict how the choice may affect self, others, and the future.
questions.explanation: Thinking about consequences helps prevent harm and supports responsible action.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain how consequences influence choices.

questions.prompt: Which source of information is most reliable when deciding how to handle a school safety concern?
options: A teacher, school policy, parent or guardian, or trained safety officer
A rumour from an unknown social media account
A joke from a class group chat
A guess based only on fear
questions.correctAnswer: A teacher, school policy, parent or guardian, or trained safety officer
questions.explanation: Reliable decisions use trustworthy sources, especially when safety is involved.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify reliable sources for making safe decisions.

questions.prompt: A learner is invited to skip class to attend an unsupervised event. What is the responsible choice?
options: Decline, remain in school, and discuss any pressure with a trusted adult
Go because friends may laugh otherwise
Lie about being sick and leave school
Share the plan only with strangers online
questions.correctAnswer: Decline, remain in school, and discuss any pressure with a trusted adult
questions.explanation: Safety, honesty, and school responsibility should guide decisions under peer pressure.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply responsible choices when facing peer pressure.

questions.prompt: A group must choose a community service activity with limited time and materials. What should they do?
options: Compare needs, resources, safety, and expected impact before choosing
Choose the activity that looks easiest in photos
Start without asking permission from relevant adults
Ignore safety because service is always harmless
questions.correctAnswer: Compare needs, resources, safety, and expected impact before choosing
questions.explanation: Good group decisions consider need, feasibility, safety, and benefit.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply decision-making criteria to group projects.

questions.prompt: A learner finds a phone at the playground. Which decision best shows integrity?
options: Hand it to a teacher or office so the owner can be found
Keep it because nobody saw it happen
Remove the SIM card and sell it
Use it to read private messages
questions.correctAnswer: Hand it to a teacher or office so the owner can be found
questions.explanation: Integrity means doing the right thing even when no one is watching.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply integrity in everyday decision-making situations.

questions.prompt: A learner must choose between immediate fun and finishing an important assignment due tomorrow. What is the best analysis?
options: Completing the assignment first protects responsibility and reduces future stress.
Immediate fun is always more important than commitments.
Assignments matter only when teachers are watching.
Future consequences should not affect present choices.
questions.correctAnswer: Completing the assignment first protects responsibility and reduces future stress.
questions.explanation: Responsible decisions weigh short-term pleasure against duties and long-term outcomes.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyze short-term and long-term effects when setting priorities.

questions.prompt: A friend asks you to share another learner's private photo. Which factor should carry the most weight?
options: Consent, dignity, safety, and possible harm to the learner
Whether sharing the photo will gain likes
Whether the friend insists it is harmless
How quickly the photo can be forwarded
questions.correctAnswer: Consent, dignity, safety, and possible harm to the learner
questions.explanation: Responsible choices protect privacy and dignity and avoid digital harm.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyze ethical factors in communication decisions.

questions.prompt: Which class plan best teaches responsible decision making?
options: Learners study a scenario, list options, predict consequences, choose safely, and reflect on the result
Learners copy one answer from the board without discussion
Learners choose actions by voting before hearing facts
Learners reward the fastest answer even when unsafe
questions.correctAnswer: Learners study a scenario, list options, predict consequences, choose safely, and reflect on the result
questions.explanation: A strong decision-making plan uses facts, options, consequences, safe action, and reflection.
questions.learningOutcome: Create a structured process for practising responsible choices.

questions.prompt: Why is it wise to seek advice before making a high-risk decision?
options: Trusted advice can reveal risks and options that the learner may have missed.
Advice makes the learner lose all responsibility.
Every adviser will choose the same answer.
High-risk choices should always be made secretly.
questions.correctAnswer: Trusted advice can reveal risks and options that the learner may have missed.
questions.explanation: Consulting trusted people can improve judgement, especially when safety or major consequences are involved.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain when and why to seek guidance before deciding.

questions.prompt: A learner is offered a shortcut to earn money by helping hide stolen items. What should they do?
options: Refuse, leave the situation safely, and report to a trusted adult or authority
Accept because quick money is always useful
Ask for a larger payment before deciding
Keep quiet so the offer continues
questions.correctAnswer: Refuse, leave the situation safely, and report to a trusted adult or authority
questions.explanation: Responsible choices avoid crime and seek help when a situation may be unsafe or unlawful.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply risk assessment to avoid unsafe or unlawful choices.

questions.prompt: A class vote is about how to use donated books. Which decision process is fairest?
options: Identify learners' needs, discuss options openly, vote transparently, and record the decision
Let the loudest learners decide privately
Give all books to one friendship group
Hide the books until people stop asking
questions.correctAnswer: Identify learners' needs, discuss options openly, vote transparently, and record the decision
questions.explanation: Fair group decisions use transparency, participation, and clear reasons.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyze fairness and transparency in shared decisions.

questions.prompt: Which decision checklist would best help learners plan a safe school trip?
options: Purpose, permission, transport safety, emergency contacts, budget, roles, and rules
Music playlist, snacks only, and a list of jokes
Names of learners who dislike planning
Only the colour of the bus
questions.correctAnswer: Purpose, permission, transport safety, emergency contacts, budget, roles, and rules
questions.explanation: A safe trip plan checks learning purpose, permission, transport, emergency preparation, resources, and responsibilities.
questions.learningOutcome: Create a decision checklist for safe group activities.

questions.prompt: Which choice best shows respect for school rules?
options: Following agreed procedures even when a shortcut seems easier
Obeying rules only when a teacher is nearby
Changing rules secretly to suit friends
Ignoring rules if they slow down a game
questions.correctAnswer: Following agreed procedures even when a shortcut seems easier
questions.explanation: Rules protect fairness and safety, so responsible learners follow them consistently.
questions.learningOutcome: Recognize responsible choices that respect agreed rules.

questions.prompt: A learner notices that a plan may benefit their group but harm another class. What is the responsible next step?
options: Raise the concern and look for an option that is fairer to both groups
Continue because only their group matters
Hide the effect until the plan is complete
Blame the other class for being affected
questions.correctAnswer: Raise the concern and look for an option that is fairer to both groups
questions.explanation: Responsible decisions consider the wellbeing and rights of others, not only personal advantage.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply ethical thinking when a choice affects other people.

questions.prompt: What is first aid?
options: Immediate basic help given to an injured or suddenly ill person before professional care
Any medicine taken without advice
A way to hide injuries from adults
A replacement for all hospital care
questions.correctAnswer: Immediate basic help given to an injured or suddenly ill person before professional care
questions.explanation: First aid gives safe immediate support while arranging proper help when needed.
questions.learningOutcome: Define first aid and its purpose.

questions.prompt: Which item belongs in a simple emergency contact list?
options: Parent or guardian, class teacher, nearby health facility, and local emergency support
Only favourite musicians
Passwords for social media accounts
A list of rumours from the neighbourhood
questions.correctAnswer: Parent or guardian, class teacher, nearby health facility, and local emergency support
questions.explanation: Emergency contacts should help a learner quickly reach trusted support.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify key emergency contacts for school and home safety.

questions.prompt: Why should medicines be taken only as directed by a qualified health worker or trusted adult?
options: Wrong use can cause harm, delay treatment, or create new health problems.
All medicines work the same for every person.
More medicine always works faster.
Medicine labels are only for decoration.
questions.correctAnswer: Wrong use can cause harm, delay treatment, or create new health problems.
questions.explanation: Medicine safety requires correct dose, timing, purpose, and guidance.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain why safe medicine use requires guidance.

questions.prompt: Why is handwashing with soap important before eating?
options: It removes many germs that can cause illness.
It makes food cook faster.
It replaces the need for clean water.
It is useful only during exams.
questions.correctAnswer: It removes many germs that can cause illness.
questions.explanation: Clean hands reduce the spread of germs from surfaces to food and the mouth.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain hygiene practices that prevent disease spread.

questions.prompt: A classmate gets a small cut while arranging chairs. What should be done first?
options: Wash hands if possible, protect yourself from blood, and inform a teacher or first aider
Touch the blood with bare hands to check the wound
Ignore it because small cuts cannot get infected
Ask classmates to crowd around the learner
questions.correctAnswer: Wash hands if possible, protect yourself from blood, and inform a teacher or first aider
questions.explanation: First aid should protect both helper and injured person and involve responsible adult support.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply safe first-aid steps for minor injuries.

questions.prompt: You smell smoke near a classroom store. What is the safest first response?
options: Alert a teacher or adult immediately and move away from danger
Open every container to find the source
Hide the smell from others
Run toward the smoke to take photos
questions.correctAnswer: Alert a teacher or adult immediately and move away from danger
questions.explanation: Fire safety requires quick reporting and moving to safety, not investigating alone.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply safe response steps when fire danger is suspected.

questions.prompt: A learner is asked by an unfamiliar motorbike rider to get on for a free ride. What should the learner do?
options: Refuse, move to a safer public place, and inform a trusted adult
Accept because free transport saves money
Give the rider home details to be polite
Invite another learner to join without checking safety
questions.correctAnswer: Refuse, move to a safer public place, and inform a trusted adult
questions.explanation: Personal safety includes refusing risky offers from unfamiliar people and seeking trusted help.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply personal safety steps when approached by unfamiliar people.

questions.prompt: A road is busy, and learners are late for school. Which choice is safest?
options: Use a marked crossing or safe point and follow traffic signals even if delayed
Run across between moving vehicles
Cross while looking only at the phone
Follow a friend without checking the road
questions.correctAnswer: Use a marked crossing or safe point and follow traffic signals even if delayed
questions.explanation: Road safety is more important than speed and requires attention to traffic rules.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyze safe choices for crossing busy roads.

questions.prompt: Which warning sign suggests that a peer may be under harmful substance influence at school?
options: Sudden confusion, unusual smell, unsafe behavior, or inability to participate normally
Asking a question in class
Carrying a clean water bottle
Choosing to sit quietly during reading time
questions.correctAnswer: Sudden confusion, unusual smell, unsafe behavior, or inability to participate normally
questions.explanation: Possible substance harm should be handled by informing a trusted adult, not by mocking or accusing.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyze signs of possible substance-related risk and safe responses.

questions.prompt: Which emergency drill plan is most complete for a school?
options: Clear alarm signal, safe routes, assembly point, role assignments, learner count, and review after practice
A loud bell only, with no route or assembly point
A race to the gate without teacher guidance
A plan kept secret until an emergency happens
questions.correctAnswer: Clear alarm signal, safe routes, assembly point, role assignments, learner count, and review after practice
questions.explanation: A complete drill prepares people, movement, accountability, and improvement after practice.
questions.learningOutcome: Create a practical emergency drill plan for school safety.

questions.prompt: Why should learners avoid sharing sharp tools during practical work without supervision?
options: Improper handling can cause injury, and supervision helps ensure safe use.
Sharp tools become safer when passed quickly.
Supervision is needed only for younger children.
Tools should be hidden from the teacher.
questions.correctAnswer: Improper handling can cause injury, and supervision helps ensure safe use.
questions.explanation: Tool safety depends on correct handling, attention, and adult guidance where needed.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain safe handling of tools during practical activities.

questions.prompt: A learner receives an online message promising gifts if they keep a meeting secret. What should they do?
options: Do not meet the sender, save the message if safe, and report to a trusted adult
Go alone because gifts are useful
Send home details to prove trust
Keep the secret to avoid disappointing the sender
questions.correctAnswer: Do not meet the sender, save the message if safe, and report to a trusted adult
questions.explanation: Secret meetings with unknown online contacts are unsafe and should be reported.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply safety rules when online contact creates real-world risk.

questions.prompt: A school is planning activities during a heavy rain season. Which risk should be considered first?
options: Flooded paths, slippery surfaces, lightning, and safe transport arrangements
The colour of learners' notebooks
Which activity looks best in photos
How to avoid all communication with parents
questions.correctAnswer: Flooded paths, slippery surfaces, lightning, and safe transport arrangements
questions.explanation: Weather-related planning should focus on hazards that could harm learners.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyze environmental hazards when planning school activities.

questions.prompt: Which safety campaign would best reduce accidents around the school gate?
options: Map risky spots, teach crossing rules, involve traffic marshals, and review incidents monthly
Tell learners to run faster across the road
Place posters only inside a locked office
Ignore boda boda and vehicle movement near the gate
questions.correctAnswer: Map risky spots, teach crossing rules, involve traffic marshals, and review incidents monthly
questions.explanation: Effective safety campaigns identify risks, teach behavior, involve responsible people, and monitor progress.
questions.learningOutcome: Create a safety campaign to reduce common school hazards.

questions.prompt: Which action helps prevent the spread of common infections in school?
options: Covering coughs and sneezes, washing hands, and staying home when advised during illness
Sharing drinking bottles with many learners
Ignoring cleaning routines
Crowding around sick learners for entertainment
questions.correctAnswer: Covering coughs and sneezes, washing hands, and staying home when advised during illness
questions.explanation: Good hygiene and responsible illness behavior protect the whole school community.
questions.learningOutcome: Recognize habits that reduce spread of common infections.

questions.prompt: What is a digital footprint?
options: The record of information a person leaves through online activity
A shoe mark made on a computer screen
A private notebook kept offline
A type of school uniform
questions.correctAnswer: The record of information a person leaves through online activity
questions.explanation: Posts, comments, searches, and shared images can form part of a person's digital footprint.
questions.learningOutcome: Define digital footprint and identify examples.

questions.prompt: Why should passwords not be shared with friends?
options: Sharing passwords can expose private information and allow misuse of accounts.
Friends always need passwords to prove loyalty.
Passwords work better when many people know them.
Sharing passwords removes all cyber risks.
questions.correctAnswer: Sharing passwords can expose private information and allow misuse of accounts.
questions.explanation: Account safety requires keeping passwords private and using secure login habits.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain why private login details must be protected.

questions.prompt: Which online message should be checked before being forwarded?
options: Any message with surprising claims, emotional language, or no clear source
Only messages written in English
Only messages sent during school hours
No messages, because forwarding is always harmless
questions.correctAnswer: Any message with surprising claims, emotional language, or no clear source
questions.explanation: Media literacy requires checking source and evidence before sharing information.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain why online information should be verified before sharing.

questions.prompt: A classmate posts an embarrassing photo of another learner without permission. What is the best response?
options: Do not share it, ask for it to be removed, and report if the harm continues
Forward it quickly before it is deleted
Add a mocking comment
Save it for future jokes
questions.correctAnswer: Do not share it, ask for it to be removed, and report if the harm continues
questions.explanation: Respectful digital citizenship protects consent, dignity, and safety.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply consent and privacy rules to online sharing.

questions.prompt: A learner receives repeated insulting messages in a class chat. What should they do?
options: Save evidence if safe, block or mute if possible, and report to a trusted adult
Reply with worse insults
Invite more learners to attack back
Delete everything and suffer silently
questions.correctAnswer: Save evidence if safe, block or mute if possible, and report to a trusted adult
questions.explanation: Cyberbullying should be handled safely with evidence, boundaries, and adult support.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply safe steps for responding to cyberbullying.

questions.prompt: Which post is most likely to harm a learner's digital reputation?
options: A public insult with personal information about another learner
A respectful reminder about a clean-up day
A school-approved poster for a debate
A thank-you message to a project team
questions.correctAnswer: A public insult with personal information about another learner
questions.explanation: Harmful public posts can damage both the target's dignity and the sender's reputation.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyze how online choices affect reputation and relationships.

questions.prompt: A learner wants to use online images in a school poster. Which choice is most ethical?
options: Use images allowed for reuse, credit the source, or create original images
Copy any image and remove the owner's name
Claim another person's artwork as original
Use private photos of classmates without asking
questions.correctAnswer: Use images allowed for reuse, credit the source, or create original images
questions.explanation: Ethical digital creation respects ownership, consent, and proper credit.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyze ethical use of digital content in learning tasks.

questions.prompt: Which digital wellbeing plan is best for exam week?
options: Set study times, limit non-essential screen use, sleep enough, and use devices for planned learning
Keep all notifications on and revise between messages
Stay online all night to avoid missing posts
Delete all learning apps and use only games
questions.correctAnswer: Set study times, limit non-essential screen use, sleep enough, and use devices for planned learning
questions.explanation: Responsible device use balances learning, rest, safety, and healthy attention.
questions.learningOutcome: Create a balanced plan for healthy and productive device use.

questions.prompt: Why should learners avoid joining unknown online groups that request personal details?
options: Such groups may misuse information or expose learners to unsafe contacts.
Unknown groups are always managed by teachers.
Personal details become safer when shared widely.
Joining every group improves privacy.
questions.correctAnswer: Such groups may misuse information or expose learners to unsafe contacts.
questions.explanation: Online safety includes protecting personal data and avoiding risky contacts.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain privacy risks when joining online groups.

questions.prompt: A learner accidentally forwards an unverified rumour. What should they do next?
options: Correct the mistake, ask others not to forward it, and verify before sharing next time
Forward more rumours so people forget the first one
Blame the person who corrected them
Delete their account without informing anyone
questions.correctAnswer: Correct the mistake, ask others not to forward it, and verify before sharing next time
questions.explanation: Repairing digital harm includes correcting misinformation and changing future behavior.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply responsible steps after causing accidental digital harm.

questions.prompt: What is community service?
options: Voluntary work that benefits people, school, or the wider community
Work done only for personal praise
A way to avoid school rules
An activity that must harm the environment
questions.correctAnswer: Voluntary work that benefits people, school, or the wider community
questions.explanation: Community service uses time and effort to improve shared wellbeing.
questions.learningOutcome: Define community service and identify its purpose.

questions.prompt: Why is caring for public property important?
options: It protects resources that many people depend on and reduces replacement costs.
It helps one person control community resources.
It is needed only when visitors are present.
It makes vandalism acceptable if nobody sees it.
questions.correctAnswer: It protects resources that many people depend on and reduces replacement costs.
questions.explanation: Public property serves many people, so caring for it shows responsibility and citizenship.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain why public property should be protected.

questions.prompt: Why should a school service project include learners with different abilities?
options: Inclusion respects dignity and allows everyone to contribute in suitable ways.
Only the fastest learners deserve roles.
Including different abilities always slows learning and should be avoided.
Service projects are for prefects only.
questions.correctAnswer: Inclusion respects dignity and allows everyone to contribute in suitable ways.
questions.explanation: Inclusive service recognizes that all learners can contribute when roles are planned fairly.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain how inclusion supports dignity in community activities.

questions.prompt: A class notices litter around the compound after lunch. What is the most responsible action?
options: Organize a safe clean-up, use bins properly, and discuss how to prevent future littering
Blame the youngest class without evidence
Kick the litter behind classrooms
Ignore it because cleaning is not learning
questions.correctAnswer: Organize a safe clean-up, use bins properly, and discuss how to prevent future littering
questions.explanation: Environmental stewardship combines action, safe practice, and prevention.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply responsible actions to care for the school environment.

questions.prompt: A learner wants to raise a concern about water wastage at school. What should they do?
options: Collect observations, propose a solution, and present it respectfully to the right school authority
Break taps to prove there is a problem
Complain online without facts
Wait for others to solve it silently
questions.correctAnswer: Collect observations, propose a solution, and present it respectfully to the right school authority
questions.explanation: Peaceful participation uses evidence, respect, and proper channels.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply respectful channels for raising community concerns.

questions.prompt: A service project is not meeting its goal because tools are missing and roles are unclear. What is the best analysis?
options: The project needs better planning, resource tracking, role allocation, and monitoring.
Community service always fails and should stop.
Learners should work harder without tools.
The goal should be kept secret from participants.
questions.correctAnswer: The project needs better planning, resource tracking, role allocation, and monitoring.
questions.explanation: Project success depends on clear goals, resources, roles, and progress checks.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyze why community projects may fail and how to improve them.

questions.prompt: Which leadership behavior best shows integrity during a class fundraiser?
options: Keeping clear records and reporting money collected to the class and teacher
Using some money secretly and returning it later
Allowing only close friends to count money
Changing records so the total looks better
questions.correctAnswer: Keeping clear records and reporting money collected to the class and teacher
questions.explanation: Integrity in leadership requires honesty, transparency, and accountability.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyze integrity and accountability in learner leadership.

questions.prompt: Which plan best supports a safe tree-planting service project?
options: Get permission, choose suitable seedlings, assign roles, carry safe tools, water seedlings, and monitor growth
Plant any tree anywhere and leave immediately
Ask only one learner to do all work
Use sharp tools without guidance to finish faster
questions.correctAnswer: Get permission, choose suitable seedlings, assign roles, carry safe tools, water seedlings, and monitor growth
questions.explanation: A strong service project includes permission, suitability, safety, roles, and follow-up.
questions.learningOutcome: Create a safe and sustainable community service project plan.

questions.prompt: Which peer education activity would best promote respectful school relationships?
options: Learners develop short role-plays on empathy, boundaries, and reporting bullying, then lead guided discussion
Learners make jokes about conflict cases from class
Learners share private stories without permission
Learners lecture others without allowing questions
questions.correctAnswer: Learners develop short role-plays on empathy, boundaries, and reporting bullying, then lead guided discussion
questions.explanation: Effective peer education is respectful, practical, participatory, and safe.
questions.learningOutcome: Create a peer education activity that promotes respectful relationships.

questions.prompt: A school committee has learners, teachers, and parents. How should learners contribute responsibly?
options: Share learners' views respectfully, listen to others, and support agreed actions
Interrupt adults until learners get everything they want
Refuse to attend meetings but complain later
Share confidential committee discussions online
questions.correctAnswer: Share learners' views respectfully, listen to others, and support agreed actions
questions.explanation: Responsible participation combines voice, respect, listening, and action.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply responsible participation in school decision-making forums.

questions.prompt: Why is budgeting useful for a class activity?
options: It helps compare costs, plan resources, and avoid waste.
It makes money appear automatically.
It removes the need for receipts.
It allows leaders to spend without explaining.
questions.correctAnswer: It helps compare costs, plan resources, and avoid waste.
questions.explanation: A budget guides spending and helps a group use available resources responsibly.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain the purpose of budgeting in group activities.

questions.prompt: A learner has KSh 200 and wants a snack, a pen, and bus fare. What should they do first?
options: Identify needs and wants, then set aside money for the most necessary items
Spend all money on snacks and borrow fare later
Buy the brightest pen without checking price
Give the money to a friend to choose for them
questions.correctAnswer: Identify needs and wants, then set aside money for the most necessary items
questions.explanation: Resource responsibility starts by separating needs from wants and prioritising essentials.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply prioritisation when using limited personal resources.

questions.prompt: A club saved money for sports equipment, but some members want to use it for a party. What is the best analysis?
options: The group should respect the original goal unless members transparently agree on a justified change.
The loudest members should spend it immediately.
Money records do not matter after collection.
A party is automatically more important than equipment.
questions.correctAnswer: The group should respect the original goal unless members transparently agree on a justified change.
questions.explanation: Financial integrity requires using funds for the agreed purpose or changing plans transparently.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyze responsible handling of shared funds.

questions.prompt: Which resource conservation plan is best for reducing waste in a classroom?
options: Track paper use, reuse clean sheets, set printing rules, recycle where possible, and review progress monthly
Hide unused paper so nobody can count it
Print every note twice to be safe
Throw away exercise books at the end of each week
questions.correctAnswer: Track paper use, reuse clean sheets, set printing rules, recycle where possible, and review progress monthly
questions.explanation: A good conservation plan measures use, changes habits, and checks whether waste is reducing.
questions.learningOutcome: Create a practical plan for conserving school resources.

questions.prompt: What is saving?
options: Keeping part of available money or resources for future use
Spending everything as soon as it is received
Borrowing more whenever money is low
Hiding group funds from the treasurer
questions.correctAnswer: Keeping part of available money or resources for future use
questions.explanation: Saving helps a person or group prepare for future needs and goals.
questions.learningOutcome: Define saving and its importance for future needs.
